_: The words a serialisation point is spelled with, handed to every refining
agent by `refine brief`. Two steps that move the same shared thing are only
held apart when they call it the same name, so the names are fixed here
rather than invented once per plan. One round produced six spellings of the
migration head across eleven steps; nothing caught it, and check would have
opened two migration-writing steps in the same round.
Extend per project with CURSOR_ORCH_POINTS=<file>, same shape. The two
lists are unioned, so a project adds without losing these.
A name may say which instance it moves, after a colon:
Two scoped names with the same class and different instances are held to be
different things, and run at the same time. Only write one where you can
point at two separate files — separate migration directories, a lockfile
per package. If they are really one shared thing, a scoped name switches
off the only gate that catches a clean merge producing a wrong tree.
A scoped name against a bare one is still one thing: a step that says plain
"lockfile" may mean all of them, so that pair is still reported.
